{# Renders the version of the docs currently being viewed, beside the logo/title in the header navbar. Why `current_version` rather than `release`: sphinx-multiversion builds every ref with the *current* checkout's conf.py, so `release` (and anything else computed in conf.py) is the same for all versions unless restored from each ref's own metadata -- and that metadata is read from each ref's *committed* conf.py, so it is empty for refs that predate this change. `current_version` comes from git and is populated per version by sphinx-multiversion, so it is correct for every documented version immediately. `current_version.release` is preferred when a ref records one; otherwise we fall back to its name (e.g. "release/0.2.0" -> "0.2.0"). `release` is the fallback for a plain single-version build, where sphinx-multiversion is not involved. The is emitted unconditionally: pydata_sphinx_theme drops navbar templates that render empty, and that check runs before sphinx-multiversion adds `current_version` to the context. Always emitting the element keeps it in the navbar; the value is filled in at final render, once `current_version` is available. #} {%- set label = "" %} {%- if current_version %} {%- set label = current_version.release or current_version.name %} {%- elif release %} {%- set label = release %} {%- endif %} {%- if label.startswith("release/") %}{% set label = label[8:] %}{% endif %} {{ label }}
